scenario: Switch the nightly jobs to a new scheduler (a decisive measurement is still pending)

motion.text: The team moves all nightly jobs to the new Quill scheduler this week.

research: Noor: Run the heavy-export benchmark Thursday (5 jobs tested so far; 8 heavy ETL jobs remain). Measure per-job and aggregate runtime, tail latency under I/O contention, and document any connection-pool or resource-isolation findings.

Axel: Run a two-night parallel canary of the six DB exports on Quill alongside the old scheduler. Record per-job minutes, lock-timeout events, memory-limit hits, and total export time vs. the 40-minute baseline. Report whether the 15-minute slack survives.
Axel / Noor: Obtain or test Quill's concurrent-pool and I/O-isolation semantics for multiple simultaneous DB-export jobs; report whether behavior is specified, tunable, or undefined.
Wen: Write and test a full rollback script (Quill → old scheduler) and validate it end-to-end by end of day Monday. Document the restore time in hours.
Wen: Monitor Noor's five validated jobs in production through one full week; report any timing drift, paging events, or manual interventions.
All: Compile a revised staged-cutover plan (5 jobs now → canary exports → remaining jobs next cycle) with explicit go/no-go gates tied to the data above, for the next meeting.

chairQuestions.topic: actual runtime of the six heavy DB exports on the current scheduler
chairQuestions.experience_sought: How many minutes does each of your six exports currently take end-to-end on the old scheduler, and what is the remaining slack in the window immediately after your last export finishes?

chairQuestions.topic: Quill's documented connection-pool and resource-isolation behavior under concurrent load
chairQuestions.experience_sought: In any testing, staging environment, or vendor documentation you have reviewed, does Quill document how it handles multiple concurrent DB-connection jobs competing for the same pool or I/O bandwidth, or is that behavior unspecified?
